profile.headline: AI Security @ Zscaler | Penn State
profile.summary:
Most engineering teams don't fail because of bad code. They fail because nobody owns the boring, load-bearing systems underneath it - the config layer every service depends on, the legacy integration held together by 40-year-old assumptions.
 
That's the work I go looking for.
 
At NetScout, I inherited a config system that worked, but every team had built its own version in isolation - nothing centralized, nothing that scaled past a single team's use case. I redesigned it from the ground up - clean APIs, clear storage abstractions, safety guardrails - into a single system now adopted by engineers working on our core platform, replacing legacy one.
 
Before that, I built a PostgreSQL wire-protocol parser from scratch for our observability and security monitoring, handling authentication, multi-packet fragmentation, and query messages end-to-end. I also reverse-engineered a 40-year-old undocumented SNMP layer with no spec and no original authors left to ask, then built a parallel REST/HTTPS path intended to eventually replace it.
 
Along the way: cut build times by 10% by hunting down redundant recompilation nobody had prioritized, and diagnosed an initialization-ordering bug mid-migration that was one bad call away from a full company-wide rollback.
 
I work in C/C++ and Python, I like systems where correctness gets checked early instead of discovered in production, and I'm currently looking at backend and infrastructure roles and own systems end-to-end.

positions.description:
Redesigned a fragmented, per-team configuration approach into a single centralized framework with unified APIs and storage abstractions. Currently rolling out across teams on the core platform, adjusting the design as teams migrate, provide suggestions and report issues.

Diagnosed an initialization-ordering bug mid-migration during a company-wide storage transition, resolving it across three platforms under a hard deadline and averting what would have been a full rollback.
 
Identified and eliminated redundant recompilation in internal build tooling, cutting build times by 10%.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Built a PostgreSQL wire-protocol parser from scratch - handling authentication, startup, termination, and query messages - engineered to separately expose server-side processing time versus total round-trip response time, giving security monitoring tools a level of measurement precision customer didn't have before.
 
Reverse-engineered a 30-year-old undocumented SNMP communication layer with no available spec, then built a parallel REST/HTTPS path with a thread-safe queue bridging HTTP and internal threads — intended to eventually replace the legacy protocol dependency.

positions.title: Graduate Research And Teaching Assistant
positions.description: Researched network-slice security vulnerabilities for a 5G master's thesis, running packet-level simulations in ns-3.

projects.title: Food AId
projects.description:
Food AId, is an AI based application, that leverages google cloud services to help Lion's Pantry. Food AId, is a team of multi-cultural and multi-disciplinary students, with the same aim to help the society. 

My role as a Technical team lead, was to develop inventory system for Lion's Pantry using App Engine and mysql. In addition to that, we also developed prediction model using TensorFlow to predict number of people coming to Lion's Pantry.
